post_run_edits.why: the `cleanup` block was inserted by hand after this run: the tool AT `code_head` has no `cleanup` builder at all (`git show 318950c6e0:tools/capstone_12186_recall.py | grep -c cleanup` = 0 — 318950c6e0 rather than the run head's sha, which the rebase made unreachable; see `code_head_note`), so reproducing at the head this record names yields every number below and no `cleanup` block. The block is a DECLARATION of the graph residue, not a figure; every figure in this record is run output. Any later run writes the block itself and records `post_run_edits: []`.

the `user_search*` arms' `door_note` PROSE was restated after the run. It read "at the MCP tool `tortoise_search`'s own defaults", which is false about two default values: the tool's own defaults are `entity_type='point'` and `limit=10` (`tortoise/mcp_server.py::tortoise_search`), while the arms call `entity_type='object'` (the population IS `:Object` names) at `limit=15`. The note now states the VERB/ARGUMENTS split instead. NO FIGURE IS AFFECTED — this is the note, not the readings; the recall/duplicate/mint figures are unchanged run output.

every paired-shaped block gained three DECLARATION fields — `ids_truncated_at` (=20, the tool's `IDS_LIMIT`), `gain_ids_truncated` and `loss_ids_truncated` — because `gain_ids`/`loss_ids` were capped at 20 while `gains`/`losses` were not, so a block publishing `gains: 43` beside 20 ids let a reader re-derive 20 as the count. The TOOL emits them from one dict, so a re-run writes them in BOTH serialisations (`paired[...]` and `merged_lever_visibility`); the committed record predates that, so the two `merged_lever_visibility` copies were patched by hand as well. No id list was changed and no FIGURE was changed: the three fields state a property of the code, and `gains`/`losses` already carried the true totals.

the field was added by hand after the run, and it is now BUILDABLE: `_code_head_note(run_head)` emits exactly this string, so a later run writes it and records `post_run_edits: []`. It exists because the branch's rebase onto `origin/main` rewrote `code_head` into a sha no published ref reaches, so the record must say that `code_head` is a LABEL and where a reproduction should actually run. Declared rather than left implicit: an edit no builder emits is an edit the ledger cannot see, which is the whole reason this list exists.

code_head_note: `code_head` 31bce52ddbb3 is the RUN head and is a LABEL, not a reproduction anchor. This branch is rebased onto `origin/main` before it lands, and a rebase rewrites 31bce52ddbb3, leaving it an ancestor of no published ref — a `git show` against it then fails with `fatal: invalid object name` for a reader without the pre-rebase object. The CONTENT is verifiable even where the sha is not: reproduce at the branch's own head — the two INPUTS this record names (`tools/capstone_12186_recall.py`'s query/recall code and `docs/evidence/12186-capstone/queries.json`, whose sha256 the `pin` block pins) are what a reproduction needs, and the tool's later changes are comments and new builder functions, never the recall computation. Read `code_head` for WHICH RUN this is; run the commands against `HEAD`. In a shallow clone, `git fetch --unshallow` first.
